title: From the Pacific to Andhra Pradesh

scenes.title:
One ocean.
A different monsoon.
scenes.voice: Andhra Pradesh's monsoon has a distant connection: the Pacific Ocean.
scenes.source: Earth imagery: NASA Blue Marble | Conceptual introduction

scenes.title:
The winds move
the warmth.
scenes.voice: Normally, trade winds push warm surface water towards Indonesia. Cold water rises near South America.
scenes.source: NOAA ENSO explanation | Circulation is schematic

scenes.chapter: El Niño / When the pattern shifts
scenes.title:
Winds weaken.
Warmth spreads east.
scenes.voice: During El Nino, trade winds weaken. Warmth spreads east and tropical rainfall shifts.
scenes.source: NOAA ERSST v5 through 2026-09 | 1991-2020 baseline | Winds schematic

scenes.title:
It has happened
before.
scenes.voice: Major events include nineteen ninety seven and twenty fifteen.
scenes.source: NOAA historical ENSO record | 1997-98 and 2015-16

scenes.chapter: The ocean now / observed and forecast
scenes.title:
The Pacific outlook.
Not AP's rainfall outlook.
scenes.voice: NOAA's July to September ocean index is plus 2.16 degrees. Its October eighth outlook projects a relative-index peak of 2.74 degrees. Strong to very strong conditions remain over eighty three percent likely through March. This is not an Andhra Pradesh rainfall forecast.
scenes.source: NOAA CPC | Observed ONI: Jul-Sep 2026 | Forecast RONI: issued 2026-10-08 | Different indices

scenes.title:
A shift in the sky.
A change in the odds.
scenes.voice: India's summer monsoon can weaken. The Indian Ocean and local weather also matter.
scenes.source: NOAA ENSO-monsoon explanation | Schematic; no local rainfall forecast

scenes.title:
A tendency.
Not a certainty.
scenes.voice: 5 of 7 El Nino summer monsoons were below average in Andhra Pradesh, averaging 13 percent below.
scenes.source: CHIRPS v3.0 project analysis | June-September, 1981-2025 | Historical association

scenes.title:
What fell
over Andhra Pradesh?
scenes.voice: June to August 2026 rainfall was 41.5 percent below average. Rank 1 driest in 46 years.
scenes.source: CHIRPS v3.0 | June to August 2026 | Comparison 1981-2026

scenes.title:
A new season.
Too early to judge.
scenes.voice: Historically, El Nino northeast monsoons averaged 7.7 percent below normal: 9 of 15 years. The north coast fared worst. This season has only just begun.
scenes.source: CHIRPS v3.0 project analysis | Oct-Dec, 1981-2025 | History, not an AP forecast

scenes.title:
The journey
below the surface.
scenes.voice: Rain infiltrates soil and fractured rock. Pumping and geology shape what remains.
scenes.source: AI-generated geological illustration | Flow is schematic; not a surveyed site

scenes.title:
The wells tell
the local story.
scenes.voice: By September, 54.3 percent of compared mandals were deeper than in May. 85.7 percent were short of their own ten year normal.
scenes.source: APWRIMS project series | 2026-05 to 2026-09 | Rebuilt State outlines + prototype fallback; not certified boundaries

scenes.title:
One state.
Uneven shortfalls.
scenes.voice: District shortfalls differ. These are medians of observations, not predictions.
scenes.source: APWRIMS project series: 2026-05 to 2026-09 | CHIRPS v3 history: 1981-2025

scenes.chapter: The State's own wells / measured snapshot
scenes.title:
The network reads
deeper water.
scenes.voice: The State's 1746 station network reads 11.43 metres below ground on September ninth, 3.18 metres deeper than a year earlier.
scenes.source: AP AWARE State groundwater feed | 2026-09-09 | Latest-reading aggregate, not a monthly mean

scenes.title:
Deeper water.
A longer reach.
scenes.voice: Orvakal reads 29.68 metres. Water is 14.61 metres deeper this season, instead of its usual 2.36 metre rise.
scenes.source: APWRIMS | Orvakal, Kurnool | 2026-05 to 2026-09 | AI illustration, not site imagery

scenes.title:
Less recharge.
More pressure on wells.
scenes.voice: Less recharge and continued pumping can increase pressure on wells.
scenes.source: Conditional risk, not a rainfall forecast or drought declaration | AI illustration

scenes.title:
A summer projection.
With a track record.
scenes.voice: Past winters project 126 mandals beyond their deepest May. 76 are already over ten metres deep, home to about sixty seven lakh people in twenty twenty. Historically, only 32.5 percent of beyond-record calls materialised.
scenes.source: Project summer outlook | Anchor 2026-09 to 2027-05 | WorldPop 2020 | Not an AP rainfall forecast

scenes.title:
Evidence for review.
Not a declaration.
scenes.voice: As of October tenth, 477 mandals meet the rainfall trigger. 30 read severe, 325 moderate. This is manual evidence, not a drought declaration.
scenes.source: Project screening against DA&FW Drought Manual 2020 | 2026-10-10 | Incomplete indicators retained

scenes.title:
Conserve today.
Prepare for a dry spell.
scenes.voice: For a possible dry spell: protect drinking water. Use drip irrigation and mulch where suitable. Agree a village contingency plan with local teams.
scenes.source: NIDM / ICAR / Jal Shakti guidance | AI illustration | Local advice, not a drought forecast

scenes.title:
Cities cannot stop El Niño.
They can reduce water stress.
scenes.voice: Cities cannot stop El Nino. Repair mains. Reuse safely treated water for non-drinking needs. Protect lakes and essential supplies.
scenes.source: MoHUA AMRUT 2.0 / NIDM guidance | AI urban illustration, not completed works

scenes.title:
Protect supplies.
Review local evidence.
scenes.voice: Read observations, NOAA's Pacific forecast, and the summer projection separately. None forecasts Andhra Pradesh rainfall. Verify locally. Assign action.
scenes.source: Proposed review, not an official directive | Well snapshot: 2026-09 | Synthetic narration; review pending

rain.product: CHIRPS v3.0 monthly, 0.05 degrees, mandal mean

volume.note: shortfall in metres of water table x the mandal's specific yield x its area; specific yield is the CGWB measurement where one exists for that mandal, otherwise the documented aquifer proxy

recharge.rule: May-to-2026-09 change against the same mandal's median over the previous 10 years; flagged short at >= 1.0 m AND >= 2.0x its own year-to-year spread

pacific.source: NOAA Extended Reconstructed SST v5; anomaly against 1991-2020
pacific.basemapSource: NASA Blue Marble Next Generation (public domain)

enso.index: Oceanic Nino Index (NOAA CPC, ERSST v6)

ocean.source: NOAA Climate Prediction Center, official ENSO outlook and ENSO Diagnostic Discussion
ocean.licence: US Government work, public domain; the synopsis is quoted verbatim
ocean.index: RONI: CPC's relative Niño 3.4 index, three-month means, 1991–2020 base
ocean.synopsis: El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance).
ocean.caveat: An El Niño forecast is a forecast for the tropical Pacific, not a rainfall forecast for Andhra Pradesh.

stateWells.source: AP AWARE groundwater feed (groundwater_aggregatedreadings_api) via the AI Living Labs data lake
stateWells.note: One recent reading per location from the State's monitoring network, not a monthly mean. Shown beside our monthly series; not merged into it and not used by the model.

summer.source: APWRIMS monthly groundwater level by mandal (Ground Water and Water Audit Department piezometers), metres below ground
summer.method: May depth = latest reading plus the mandal's own past drawdowns from the same month to May: typical = median, dry winter = largest on record. Risk against the deepest May on record in the same series.

people.source: WorldPop (University of Southampton) 2020 population counts, 1 km, UN-adjusted, India; summed over each mandal outline at 250 m

manual.title: Manual for Drought Management (updated 2020)
manual.publisher: Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India
